implementation_notes: A case class generates `copy(name = value)` with a default for every constructor parameter plus product accessors and equality, so a one-level update is an expression and depth nests: `p.copy(home = p.home.copy(city = "Berlin"))`. That replaces the hand-written setter cascade with generated code at no dependency cost, and `val` fields keep the value immutable. Because `copy` cannot be stored, passed or composed, the classic composed form (Monocle optics or hand-written getter/setter lambdas) is justified when the same deep focus is referenced by many modules or derived dynamically.
pitfalls: `copy` is shallow: mutable collections, `var` fields and arrays inside the case class stay shared between the copies, so the immutability is only as deep as the field types.
Every nesting level needs its own `copy` call - an intermediate that is not a case class (a plain class or a Java type) has no generated copy and silently forces in-place mutation.
Case-class equality and hashCode come from the constructor parameters, so a class with extra mutable state compares equal while behaving differently.

variants.name: Monocle Lens / GenLens composition
variants.implementation_notes: Monocle is the standard optics library of the Scala ecosystem: `Lens[Address, Int](_.streetNumber)(n => a => a.copy(streetNumber = n))` builds the getter/setter pair - `GenLens[Person](_.age)` derives the same optic from an accessor lambda - and `compose` chains lenses so a deep path becomes one value. Setter-like optics expose `replace`/`modify` and return an endofunction `S => S`, which is what lets a path be passed around, stored in a config or reused across modules; for a single nested update, plain `copy` is still simpler and dependency-free.
variants.code_sketch:
import monocle.Lens
import monocle.macros.GenLens

val home: Lens[Person, Address] = GenLens[Person](_.home)
val city: Lens[Address, String] = GenLens[Address](_.city)

val homeCity = home.compose(city)
homeCity.get(p)                    // 'London'
homeCity.replace("Berlin")(p)      // new person
homeCity.modify(_.toUpperCase)(p)
pitfalls: Composition arrows are easy to get wrong: `compose` takes an optic whose source is this optic's target, and mixing it up with `andThen`/direction errors surfaces as confusing type mismatches.

A composed `Lens` is a value: renaming a case-class field updates `GenLens` call sites at compile time, but a hand-written `Lens` built from lambdas keeps compiling until the setter silently targets the wrong field.
Monocle targets Scala 2.12/2.13 with Cats and a separate Scala 3 module: mixing artifacts is the usual cause of "works in tests, fails on the build server".
